text:
anya: Heads-up — after yesterday's continuous-batching change (PR #8421) I'm seeing prefix cache hit rate drop on prod for chat-short prompts. Hit rate went from ~22% -> ~7% on p4d pool. Latencies up for 0-3 token responses. Anyone else?

mike: saw alerts. Querying per-route stats now.

perf-bot: Profiling snapshot for model=redwood/open-chat-3-small, region=us-east-1, pool=dedicated-p4d
```
prefix_cache.hit_rate: 0.072
avg_lat_ms (1st_token): 180.4 -> 240.9
avg_lat_ms (subseq): 12.2 -> 18.6
batch_size_mean: 6.1 -> 9.8
composition_shift: more mixed prefixes per batch
```

jess: Noticed similar on staging after enabling "aggressive continuous batching". Could be batch composition causing different key coalescing? If batches mix requests with different prefixes, prefix-KV reuse drops.

kai: Quick note: our cache key currently uses canonicalized prefix token ids + request model variant + truncation window. If batching reorders queries and we send different context lengths, KV cache warming may not line up. Related to PR that removed prefix-preserving batching.

anya: Good point. The PR allowed continuous batching to merge "short" and "long" requests eagerly to increase throughput. Hypothesis: more mixed-length batches mean many short-prefix requests no longer see own warmed KV in tail workers.

mike: I ran a flamegraph from the runtime tracer — seems a lot of time in kv.fetch() and kernel fallback from cuBLAS->fused-kernel due to different seq_len in a batch.

perf-bot: recent trace snippet:
```
TRACE: batch_id=2257 seq_lens=[4,96,8,120,5,6,7,90,3]
KV_FETCH miss_rate: 0.65
kernel_select: fallback_path=fused_attention_slow
```

sam: Possible mitigations:
- prefer prefix-homogeneous batch composition (group by prefix-hash)
- warmup policy: schedule a "priming" request to same worker for expected prefixes
- change cache key to be less strict on trailing pad tokens

jess: Can we simulate cost/latency tradeoffs? More homogeneous batches might reduce avg batch size and throughput.

anya: I ran a simple sim: if we constrain composition to same-prefix groups, hit_rate -> ~0.28 but throughput drops ~12%. Latency p50 for tokens down 30ms.

mike: Also need to consider queueing: holding requests longer to assemble homogeneous batch increases head latency for first token. For PLG endpoints that hurts UX.

kai: Proposal:
1) Revert aggressive merge for short/long requests in continuous batching and introduce prefix-aware shaper with 200ms max-hold.
2) Add lightweight prefix hash header in router to prefer co-location with existing KV warm entries.
3) Add an opt-in warmup flag in model config to send a common priming request on worker spin-up and after eviction.

jess: +1 to 1 and 2. For 3, check memory pressure: priming every spin-up could bloat cache.

anya: I'll prepare a microbenchmark PR to test prefix-aware shaper with param sweep (hold=50/100/200ms) and a metric dashboard for hit-rate vs throughput.

mike: I'll triage PR for reverting merge; add an A/B to 10% traffic to measure.

infra-bot: deploy check: canary slot available in us-east-1-p4d. Remember to update rollout config.

anya: Thanks. Filing follow-up issue: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INF-1247

jess: tagging SLO owners @slo-team for visibility :eyes:

kai: FYI: also check kernel selection thresholds — if fused kernel slower for mixed seqs, maybe better to force per-sample seq pad ordering.

anya: Great. We'll sync tomorrow 9:30am PT in eng-runtime channel with microbench results.

mike: noted. :thumbsup:
